title: Best Water Purifier Under Rs 15,000 in India (2026): RO+UV Picks
description: We compared 8 water purifiers under Rs 15,000 in India: Kent, A.O. Smith, Pureit, Eureka Forbes. RO+UV+UF, 7-10L storage, TDS controller. 4 picks + 1 skip.

headings.text: What actually matters in a water purifier under Rs 15,000
RO vs UV: which technology do you need
What to do with RO reject water

cta.headline: Safe drinking water without the premium price?
cta.sub: A Rs 15,000 RO+UV water purifier with 7-10L storage and TDS controller is the right shape for Indian homes. We ranked 8 models for purification quality, storage capacity, and annual filter cost.

faq.q: How much water does an RO purifier waste?
faq.a: Standard RO purifiers waste 3-4 litres of reject water per 1 litre of purified water (75% rejection rate). Newer water-saving RO purifiers (Kent Eco, Pureit Eco) achieve 2:1 ratio -- 2 litres reject per 1 litre purified. The reject water is not dirty -- it is slightly hard water suitable for mopping, gardening, or washing. Do not drink reject water. Use it for plants or cleaning.

faq.q: What is the best TDS for drinking water?
faq.a: BIS standard: 100-200 TDS is ideal. Under 100 TDS = flat taste, no minerals. 200-500 TDS = acceptable but tastes hard. Over 500 TDS = unsafe for long-term consumption (kidney stones, hypertension risk). RO purifier output should be 50-150 TDS. The TDS controller blends some raw water back to hit the 100-200 sweet spot. Without TDS controller, RO output is 20-50 TDS (flat taste).

faq.q: How often should filters be replaced?
faq.a: Sediment pre-filter: every 6 months (Rs 200-400). Carbon pre-filter: every 12 months (Rs 400-600). RO membrane: every 2-3 years (Rs 1,500-2,500). UV lamp: every 1-2 years (Rs 500-800). Most purifiers have filter-life indicators. Annual filter cost: Rs 2,500-3,500 for the 4 picks above. Without regular filter changes, bacteria grow in the pre-filter and contaminate the purified water.

faq.q: Can RO water be used for cooking rice and dal?
faq.a: Yes, but mineral content is lower. RO water is fine for tea, coffee, dal, curry. For chapati dough, RO water sometimes makes the dough feel slimsy (low calcium). If your chapati dough feels off with RO water, blend in 10-20% tap water for the dough only. Do not use reject water for cooking.

faq.q: Do I need a water purifier if my municipal water is clean?
faq.a: Even clean municipal water can pick up contaminants in the pipeline to your home (old pipes, biofilm, intermittent contamination during pipe repairs). The 4 picks above provide a safety net. For Mumbai/Kolkata municipal water (low TDS, chlorinated), UV-only is sufficient and saves the RO reject water waste. For Delhi/Chennai/Bangalore/Hyderabad (high TDS, intermittent contamination), RO+UV is essential.

tldr_pick: Our top pick is the Kent Grand Plus (11014). RO+UV+UF triple purification, 8L storage for families of 4-5, TDS controller for mineral retention, 5-stage pre-filtration extends RO membrane life to 3+ years, and Kent service network is the widest in India. Best balance of brand reliability, purification quality, and price at Rs 12,499.
key_takeaways: RO+UV is essential for Delhi/Chennai/Bangalore/Hyderabad tap water.
7-10L storage is the right size for families of 4-5.
TDS controller preserves minerals and improves taste.
Annual filter cost is Rs 2,500-3,500 -- budget for it.
who_for: Indian families who want safe drinking water without paying Rs 20,000-30,000 for premium imported brands. Ideal for homes with high-TDS municipal water (Delhi, Chennai, Bangalore, Hyderabad), borewell-dependent homes, and families of 4-5 who need 7-10L storage.
methodology: We compared 8 water purifiers available on Amazon India, Flipkart, and brand stores under Rs 15,000. For each, we evaluated purification technology (RO/UV/UF/Mineral), storage capacity, flow rate, stages of filtration, TDS controller presence, warranty, and service network. Cross-referenced long-term reliability from Indian home appliance forums.
